title: Regression to the Mean
hook: Your best month ever probably won't repeat, and that doesn't mean you did something wrong.
statement: Extreme results are mostly luck, and luck doesn't repeat. Expect things to drift back toward normal.
explainer: Results mix skill and chance. A crazy high or low month got a push from luck that won't come back. So don't overreact to peaks or panic at dips.
sop: Pick the result you're reacting to.
Find the long-run Mean across many periods.
Estimate the Correlation between one period and the next, from 0 to 1.
Calculate Expected Next before you plan around the spike.
Judge any change against that baseline, not the peak.
equation_example: Mean 100, Observed 150, Correlation 0.4. 100 + 0.4 × (150 - 100) = 100 + 20 = 120. Higher Correlation keeps the forecast close to the standout result. Lower pulls it back toward 100, meaning the spike was mostly luck.
question: Take your best month this year and write down what a normal month really looks like.
closing_statement: Know how much of your best and worst was just the dice.
caption:
Principle Nº 350: Regression to the Mean

Your best month ever probably won't repeat, and that doesn't mean you did something wrong.

Extreme results are mostly luck, and luck doesn't repeat. Expect things to drift back toward normal.

Your turn: Take your best month this year and write down what a normal month really looks like.
